html:
The Spanish-Chamorro Wars were fought from 1671 to 1695 between Chamorros and Spanish forces in Guam and the Mariana Islands, after the Jesuit Diego Luis de San Vitores founded a mission in 1668.

San Vitores baptised thousands, but tensions grew over his ways and over Spanish soldiers. In 1672 he was killed by the chief Mataʻpang, and Spain answered with years of war. Disease killed far more than fighting.

By the end, the Chamorro population had fallen to a few thousand, and survivors were moved into Catholic villages on Guam. The latte villages were abandoned. Guam became a stop for the Manila galleons and stayed Spanish until the US capture of 1898.
sum: The Spanish-Chamorro Wars were fought from 1671 to 1695 between Chamorros and Spanish forces in Guam and the Mariana Islands, after the Jesuit Diego Luis de San Vitores founded a mission in 1668.
